description: Reproduced from user zip (bw-repro). go-git v5.17.0 (and upstream main) storage/filesystem/dotgit/dotgit.go objectPacks() only discovers packs named pack-<hash>.pack. C git reads any *.idx in objects/pack. git's 'loose-objects' maintenance task (daily under maintenance.strategy=incremental, enabled by 'git maintenance start'/'register' and Scalar) writes loose-<hash>.pack. Run 1 packs loose objects but leaves them on disk (bw still works); run 2 prune-packed deletes the loose copies -> objects exist only in loose-*.pack -> bw sees 'object not found' (sync: 'walk remote commits: object not found'; list: 'open treefs: read commit: object not found'). NOT caused by geometric repack or gc --auto (verified: those only write pack-*). Workaround: git repack -a -d (verified on both repos); prevent recurrence with git config maintenance.loose-objects.enabled false. Fix options: (a) detect non-pack- packs on open and error with actionable message / auto-repack via execGit; (b) patch go-git pack discovery (needs path-based API, objectPackPath builds pack-<hash>). Related: bw-gh-138 (stale handle after fetch, different).

comments.text: Upstream: go-git issue #2345 (2026-08-26) is this exact bug. PR #2346 (2026-08-27) fixes it but targets main/v6, is 47 files +2811/-1895 tangled with a packhandle refactor, CONFLICTING, no reviews, no v5 backport. bw is on v5.17.0; latest v5.19.2 and v6.0.0-alpha.5 still filter on pack- prefix. Waiting on upstream is not viable. Plan: billy fs shim in bw that aliases loose-<hash>.{pack,idx} as pack-<hash>.* for go-git's dotgit discovery; delete when an adoptable go-git release fixes discovery.

Upstream fix drafted and submitted: https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2390 (draft), targeting go-git releases/v5.x, from fork jallum/go-git branch fix/loose-pack-discovery. TDD: added TestObjectPacksLooseNamed + TestDeleteOldObjectPackAndIndexLooseNamed to storage/filesystem/dotgit (red against upstream master, green after fix). Fix recognizes loose- alongside pack- in objectPacks discovery, objectPackOpen (tries both prefixes), and DeleteOldObjectPackAndIndex (resolves actual on-disk prefix before stat/remove). Full go-git test suite + go vet pass. Diff is 128+/13- across dotgit.go + dotgit_test.go only -- deliberately independent of the much larger v6-only PR #2346. Once merged and tagged upstream, bump bw's go.mod (currently go-git v5.17.0) to the fixed v5.x release; until then bw's own workaround (git repack -a -d + disable maintenance.loose-objects) still applies.

Verified the upstream fix (go-git/go-git PR #2390, fork jallum/go-git@fix/loose-pack-discovery) against bw itself: built bw from a scratch worktree with 'go mod edit -replace github.com/go-git/go-git/v5=<patched fork>', then reran both reproductions.
1) User's zip repro (bw-repro/repro.sh): bw sync now says 'up to date' instead of 'error: walk remote commits: object not found'.
2) Real-world trigger, rebuilt from scratch: a fresh bw repo, 40 issues, then `git maintenance run --task=loose-objects` run twice (2nd run prunes the loose copies, leaving objects only in loose-*.pack). Ran a 3rd time too, for a repo whose .git/objects/pack/ contains ONLY loose-*.pack files, zero pack-*. With the patched binary: bw list, bw create, and bw sync all work at every stage.
Confirms the PR fixes bw's actual failure mode, not just the synthetic repro. Next: wait on upstream review of #2390; once merged/tagged, bump go.mod. No further action needed to validate the fix itself.
Follow-up ticket beadwork-ic3: pin bw's go.mod to the fork (jallum/go-git@bw-pin) with a regression test, as a stopgap until go-git/go-git#2390 merges upstream.

title: [BUG] go-git ignores loose-*.pack written by git maintenance loose-objects task; bw fails with object not found
